children: , the Dutch semiconductor-equipment heavyweight, scored a massive 2,350 price target from UBSroughly 61.7% above Tuesday's Amsterdam close. Wall Street was not celebrating yet. ASML's U.S.-listed shares fell approximately 1.6% to $1,669.47 as climbing bond yields hit technology stocks.

UBS analyst Francois-Xavier Bouvignies thinks investors are overplaying the threat from China. Chinese manufacturers are closing gaps in older deep-ultraviolet machines, but ASML still owns the commercial extreme-ultraviolet battlefield. The numbers back that dominance: second-quarter sales hit 9.3 billion, while gross margin reached 54% and net income landed at 2.9 billion.

The revenue outlook has also exploded higher. ASML now expects 43 billion to 45 billion for the year, smashing its original 34 billion-to-39 billion range. Still, the picture flashes a valuation warning: the $1,669.47 share price sits 32.48% above its $1,260 GF Value estimate. UBS sees EUV pricing power and AI demand winning the race, but export restrictions, customer concentration and a premium valuation leave almost no room for execution mistakes.

title: ASML Scores 2,350 UBS Target With 61.7% Upside
